scenes.title: A problem is a starting point
scenes.visual: Founder reviews anonymous problem and customer cards.
scenes.narration: A problem describes a difficulty. An opportunity hypothesis describes a useful improvement you might help a specific group achieve. It is a direction to investigate, not proof that a business should exist. Keep the people, task and context from your discovery work.

scenes.title: Name the desired outcome
scenes.visual: Editable person, context and outcome cards.
scenes.narration: What would become easier, clearer or more reliable for the person? Finding registration with confidence is an outcome. Building an app is a possible means. Describe the improvement without locking in a feature or technology before you understand what is needed.

scenes.title: Use evidence honestly
scenes.visual: Founder separates reported notes from planned research.
scenes.narration: Review what you know about the difficulty, consequences and current workarounds. Keep sources and limitations visible. If your research is only planned, say so. Do not claim that an outcome is important, frequent or costly without evidence. Completing a research plan does not make its expected findings true.

scenes.title: Respect existing approaches
scenes.visual: Illustrative visitor gets helpful directions from staff.
scenes.narration: Existing approaches may already work well. What improvement might matter beyond what people do today, and what burden could change create? A possible opportunity can disappear if the current workaround is sufficient. A difficulty does not establish willingness to switch or pay.

scenes.title: Write a provisional statement
scenes.visual: Editable opportunity statement assembled in post.
scenes.narration: Use a simple statement: for this group in this context, there may be an opportunity to improve this outcome because of this specific difficulty. Name your evidence status and key unknown. Leave solutions open. Record the strongest reason this opportunity may not be worth pursuing.

scenes.title: Choose the next check
scenes.narration: Create your Opportunity Statement and Evidence Map. Include the group and problem, desired outcome, current approaches, evidence limits, provisional statement, counterargument and next check. Keep the opportunity revisable. Next you will draft a first value proposition as another hypothesis to test.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Describe an improvement before choosing a product.

children: A
problem
is a difficulty in a specific context. An
outcome
is what the person wants to achieve. A
solution
is a possible way to help. An
opportunity hypothesis
connects the group, difficulty and potential improvement; it remains unproven.
Illustrative example:

“First-time visitors may need clearer ways to locate registration before a session” leaves room for signs, staff processes or other approaches. “Build a registration app” commits to a means before establishing what helps. Neither statement proves demand.
Build the case carefully
Use a specific group, task and context from discovery.
Describe the difficulty and desired outcome separately.
Review evidence and current approaches, including what already works.
Write an improvement hypothesis without unsupported promises.
Name the strongest counterargument and next uncertainty to check.

Research planned in Lesson 15 is not research completed. Keep planned information labeled. Do not invent frequency, cost, time saved, willingness to switch or payment intent. A sufficient workaround may mean the opportunity is weak or needs reframing.
A useful statement structure
“For [group] in [context], there may be an opportunity to improve [outcome] because of [specific difficulty]. Our current basis is [source/status]; we still need to check [uncertainty].”
A statement is a thinking tool, not a market claim. Keep the solution open and record when you would refine or pause.
Review problem selection
Review landscape map
Review research plan

Try four scripted guidance modes. The preview reads your current worksheet locally; it does not send information anywhere.

replies.teach: Separate problem, outcome and solution. Describe a provisional improvement for a specific group with honest evidence limits.
replies.guide: Connect group/context, difficulty, outcome, current approaches and sources. Write an opportunity hypothesis with a counterargument and next check.
replies.review: Opportunity Statement check: {missing} required fields still empty. This scripted check counts fields only; it cannot verify evidence, benefits, switching or demand.
replies.challenge: Is your outcome a feature? Are planned findings treated as facts? Is the workaround sufficient? What would make you refine or pause?
